environment: **Organization**: none — individual developer. **Primary use of Claude Code**: software development, plus managing Claude Code's own dotfiles/config.
**Org-specific CLIs**: none. Routine CLIs are git, npm, gh, node, supabase, claude — all generic tooling.
**Internal sharing / snippet hosting**: none configured. Public paste and gist services stay outside the trust boundary.

Repo: sunbreak-pro/claude-dotfiles (private, github.com) — Claude Code's own global config. Routine git / npm / gh operations inside its working directory are in scope. Private visibility clears confidential material for this repo only; it never clears secrets or credentials.

Repo: sunbreak-pro/life-editor (PUBLIC, github.com) — React/TypeScript + Supabase personal-OS app, packaged with Electron/Capacitor. Public visibility means only this repo's own work may be pushed there; secrets and personal data are never cleared by visibility.
**Cloud provider(s)** (life-editor only): Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Realtime) and Cloudflare (CI secrets CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID / CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN).
**Key internal services** (life-editor only): the Supabase project this repo uses, reached via LIFE_EDITOR_SUPABASE_URL / LIFE_EDITOR_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY.

**Secrets management**: local .env files only — .env, .env.local, .env.*.local and supabase/.env are gitignored and must never be committed or pushed. CI secrets (CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, VITE_SUPABASE_URL) are referenced by name only in GitHub Actions.

**Sensitive data locations & audiences**: the .env files above, plus anything matched by the dotfiles .gitignore (.credentials.json, *credentials*, *.key, .env*). Personal life-tracking data held in life-editor's Supabase Postgres is personal data — share only with the user themselves.
**Protected deployment namespaces / environments**: none configured for either repo, so the `prod` / `production` heuristic under Sensitive remote targets applies unchanged.
